gaps.sentence: I didn't mean ___ you — it was a joke.
gaps.explanation: mean (= intend) takes the to-infinitive: didn't mean to upset. (mean + -ing = involve.)

gaps.sentence: I saw him ___ the wall and disappear into the garden.
gaps.explanation: see/hear + object + bare infinitive = the complete action; -ing = the action in progress. Both readings possible here; the bare infinitive is expected.

gaps.sentence: We mustn't miss ___ this exhibition — it ends on Sunday.
She left the room without ___ goodbye.
If you keep ___ like this, you'll exhaust yourself.
gaps.explanation: keep (+ on) is followed by -ing: keep working.

gaps.sentence: We managed ___ everyone before the storm hit.
Remember ___ your passport to the airport.
gaps.explanation: remember + to-infinitive = not forget to do something.

gaps.sentence: I can't imagine ___ in a tiny village again.
